name: Supabase SaaS project
summary: A public audit lab that reproduces launch-blocking Supabase failures on synthetic data and shows the evidence before and after each fix.
challenge: Teams launching on Supabase rarely know whether their row-level security, storage rules and webhooks hold up until real users find out. The lab had to show that risk and its fix in a form a buyer can read and an engineer can reproduce, without touching any real system.

decisions.title: Reproducible evidence
decisions.detail: Scenarios run against an isolated local PostgreSQL fixture and are replayed from a committed transcript. A digest ties the transcript to that exact fixture, so a hand edit fails its own check, and CI re-records it from a clean database.

decisions.title: Before and after the fix
decisions.detail: Each finding is shown as found, then re-tested after the documented fix. Untested checks never count as passes, and every result carries its scope and limitations.

decisions.title: No live database for evidence
decisions.detail: The published app holds no database connection for its evidence and runs no new query. The only writes are inquiries, stored behind tested grants and row-level security and redacted after 12 months.

detail: Four scenarios cover authorization and RLS, storage and configuration, webhook integrity, and reliability and recovery. Everything runs on synthetic data, and the lab states plainly that it is not a certification or a penetration test.
role: Solo build: I engineered, built, deployed and set up this project.
